mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is interpreted by markets as a signal of tightening financial conditions, which compresses equity discount rates and reduces expected future cash flows, thereby driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat when FEDFUNDS > 4% for at least 4 consecutive months prior to the prediction window.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, prompting risk-on sentiment that pushes S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-positive despite persistent labor strength indicators (e.g., 4 consecutive months of PAYEMS > previous month and UNRATE declines).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% month-over-month at the decision point indicates accelerating supply-side demand, which markets interpret as a bullish structural trend, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a 50-day moving average baseline with a statistically significant negative alpha (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 2% in the prior month, it triggers a risk-off reaction as markets anticipate tighter policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the identified inflation spike period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 1-year real yield (inferred from the inverse of FEDFUNDS relative to CPIAUCSL) suggests monetary accommodation, which expands the present value of expected corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns fail to outperform a 30-day rolling average by at least 1% with a 95% confidence interval.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in layoffs indicates labor market resilience, which fuels optimism about future wage growth and corporate expansion, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite sustained job openings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the goods price index (implied by INDPRO falling below 100) suggests soft demand or supply chain disruptions, which can create uncertainty and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 2.5% for three consecutive months in a tightening cycle regime, it reflects accommodative policy that lowers real borrowing costs, expanding equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a 30-day rolling average by more than 2% with a 90% confidence interval.
